title: Meeting Albert Glenn and Hope's Hall
summary: Parker recalls Albert Glenn rooming with his father when Parker was a boy, and being taken to a dance hall.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: When did you first know Glennie? Huh? When did you first know Albert Glennie?

Oh, yeah, I was a kid. I was in the country. My father was a brakeman on a train, you see? And he lived up there. Well, that brought me, brought all us up here. Well, he had a great big room in place. And Albert Glenn used to room with him, don't you know?
And that's how I come to know him.
Well, how old were you? You say he took you to a dance hall?
Oh, he's old at that. Put all that up. Put everything. Ain't no pants down, no.
No. We can find him, find him. Somewhere. Yeah. But you were a little boy, you say? Uh-huh.
I was a quite a young boy, you know?

I was going to school. And I come up here. And Albert Glennie was living in the yard with my daddy. Just like my daddy lived in front of you. All in the back of that house, you know? Uh-huh. And he lived there. Yeah, I was a friend. I know what he was doing.
And where did he take you? Which dance hall did you say it was he took you to?
Which dance hall did he take you to?
To dance? To dance hall? Yes. Oh, right there, that church over there. See that big church there? Yes. Well, that was a hall.
Called it the copperhead, the hope's hall. The hope's hall? Hope's hall. See? Now it's a back to church. Brother from my home.
